results.name: Resistance Band One Leg Kickback (Bent Position)
instructions: Start standing with a loop resistance band around your ankles. Bend forward at your hips, keeping your back straight, and place your hands on an incline bench's top edge for support.
Engage your glutes and lift your right leg off the floor, reaching as high as possible while keeping it straight.
Slowly return your right leg to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left leg.
tips: Exhale as you kick your leg back and inhale as you return it to the starting position.
Use a resistance band that provides enough tension to challenge your muscles without compromising form.
Keep your upper body straight and avoid rounding your back.
results.description: Resistance Band One Leg Kickback (Bent Position) is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

results.name: Resistance Band Reverse Hyper With Stability Ball on Flat Bench
instructions: Place a flat bench in front of you and lie face down on the bench with your hips on the edge and your legs extended straight behind you. Place a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees, and a stability ball between your feet.
Grip the sides of the bench for stability and ensure the stability ball is secure between your feet.
Engage your core and glutes, then lift your legs upward, squeezing your glutes and keeping your legs straight.
Slowly lower your legs back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep a firm grip on the sides of the bench to maintain stability.
Focus on lifting with your glutes and not using momentum.
Maintain a steady breathing rhythm, exhaling as you lift and inhaling as you lower your legs.
results.description: Resistance Band Reverse Hyper With Stability Ball on Flat Bench is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Abdominals.

results.name: Resistance Band Seated Bent Knee Abduction
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs bent at a 90-degree angle and your feet flat on the floor. Place a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees.
Engage your core, lean slightly back, and place your hands on the floor behind you for support.
Press your knees outward against the resistance of the band, spreading your legs as wide as possible while keeping your feet flat on the floor.
Slowly bring your knees back together to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you press your knees outward and inhale as you bring them back together.
Keep your feet flat on the floor and avoid lifting them off the floor.
Focus on engaging your hip abductors and glutes throughout the movement.
results.description: Resistance Band Seated Bent Knee Abduction is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abductors (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

results.name: Resistance Band Seated Hip Abduction
instructions: Sit on a bench with your legs bent at a 90-degree angle, feet slightly off the floor, and a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees. Place your hands on the bench for support.
Engage your core and sit up straight, keeping your back neutral.
Press your knees outward against the resistance of the band, opening your legs as wide as possible while keeping your feet slightly elevated.
Slowly bring your knees back together to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you press your knees outward and inhale as you bring them back together.
Keep your feet slightly off the floor to maintain consistent tension.
Focus on engaging your hip abductors and glutes throughout the movement.
results.description: Resistance Band Seated Hip Abduction is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abductors (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

results.name: Resistance Band Side Plank Glute Raise
instructions: Place a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees. Begin by lying on your left side with your legs bent at 90 degrees and stacked on top of each other.
Prop yourself up on your left forearm, ensuring your elbow is directly under your shoulder. Engage your core and lift your hips slightly off the floor.

Keeping your legs bent, lift your top leg upwards against the resistance of the band while also raising your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your leg and hips back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other side.
tips: Focus on engaging your glutes and hip abductors throughout the movement.
Exhale as you lift your leg and hip, and inhale as you lower it back down.
Maintain a steady pace to ensure consistent tension in the muscles.
results.description: Resistance Band Side Plank Glute Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Abductors.

results.name: Resistance Band Squat Jump
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees. Keep your chest up and bring both hands close to your chest.
Lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back as if you are sitting in a chair.
Explosively jump up by pushing through your heels extending your legs fully and reaching your arms upward.
Land softly back into the squat position, absorbing the impact through your legs. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Land softly with your knees slightly bent to reduce impact on your joints.
Perform the movement with control, especially when landing, to maximize muscle activation and reduce injury risk.
Exhale as you jump up and inhale as you lower into the squat.
results.description: Resistance Band Squat Jump is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Abductors.

results.name: Resistance Band Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees. Keep your chest up and bring both hands close to your chest.
Lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back as if you are sitting in a chair.
Push through your heels to stand back up to the starting position, keeping the resistance band taut.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your chest up and lean slightly forward to maintain proper form.
Ensure your knees stay in line with your toes and do not collapse inward.
Exhale as you stand up and inhale as you lower into the squat.
results.description: Resistance Band Squat is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Abductors, Core.

results.name: Resistance Band Standing Glute Kickback (Band at Knees)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees. Place your hands on your hips for balance.
Shift your weight onto your right leg and lift your left foot slightly off the floor.
Keeping your right leg straight, kick it back and upward against the band's resistance, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Slowly return your left leg to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the right leg.
tips: Maintain a slight bend in your standing leg for balance.
Exhale as you kick your leg back and inhale as you return it to the starting position.
Use a resistance band that provides enough tension to challenge your muscles without compromising form.
results.description: Resistance Band Standing Glute Kickback (Band at Knees) is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the balance category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

results.name: Resistance Band Standing Glute Kickback (Band at Ankles)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a loop resistance band around your ankles. Place your hands on your hips for balance.
Shift your weight onto your right leg and lift your left foot slightly off the floor.
Keeping your right leg straight, kick it back and upward against the band's resistance, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Slowly return your left leg to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the right leg.
tips: Maintain a slight bend in your standing leg for balance.
Exhale as you kick your leg back and inhale as you return it to the starting position.
Use a resistance band that provides enough tension to challenge your muscles without compromising form.
results.description: Resistance Band Standing Glute Kickback (Band at Ankles) is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the balance category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

results.name: Resistance Band Standing Balance Hip Abduction
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees. Place your hands on your hips for balance.
Shift your weight onto your right leg and lift your left foot slightly off the floor.
Keeping your left leg straight, lift it to the side against the band's resistance, squeezing your hip abductors at the top of the movement.
Slowly return your leg to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the right leg.
tips: Exhale as you lift your leg and inhale as you return it to the starting position.
Maintain a slight bend in your standing leg for balance.
Keep your upper body straight and avoid leaning to the side.
results.description: Resistance Band Standing Balance Hip Abduction is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abductors (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the balance category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Core.
